events.summary:
The Flood Advisory will expire at 11 PM PDT this evening for a
portion of Southwest California, including the following areas,
Orange and San Diego.

The heavy rain has ended. Urban area and small stream flooding is no

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1045 AM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in creeks and normally dry washes is
imminent or occurring. Dangerous flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1048 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Overflowing poor drainage areas will cause minor
flooding in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Big Bug Creek, Agua Fria River, Black Canyon, Turkey Creek,
Castle Creek, Humbug Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Black Canyon City, Dewey-Humboldt, Cordes Lakes, Mayer, Spring
Valley, Crown King, Agua Fria National Monument, Poland Junction,
Lake Pleasant, Cordes Junction, Castle Hot Springs, Arcosanti,
Horse Thief Basin, Bumble Bee, Rock Springs, Cleator, Humbug,
Coles Bay and Humbug Bay.
- This includes the following highways...
State Route 69 between mile markers 263 and 283. Interstate 17
between mile markers 242 and 268.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Turney Gulch Group Campground, Hazlett Hollow Campground and
Black Canyon Campground.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

inches possible. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph. Blowing snow
possible.

events.summary:
FFWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Washington Parish in southeastern Louisiana...
West Central Pearl River County in southern Mississippi...

* Until 200 AM CST.

* At 1250 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 4 and 8 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Bogalusa.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Gila County in east central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Tonto Creek and flood-prone locations is
occurring. Low-water crossings are inundated with water and may not
be passable. Tonto Creek is expected to continue to slowly rise
over the next 12-24 hours.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1026 PM MST, a streamflow gauge on Tonto Creek north of Tonto
Basin is above action stage, with a stage height of 4.38 feet at
915 PM MST. Flooding is ongoing along Tonto Creek in the warned
area. Please use the Tonto Creek Bridge for all travel across the
creek. Bar X Crossing, and any other low water crossings, will
likely become impassable.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Tonto Basin.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Monday evening. .

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Castle Country; San Rafael Swell; Lower Washington County; Zion National Park; Southern Mountains; Bryce Canyon Country; South Central Utah; Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity; Western Canyonlands; Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, San Rafael Swell, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef
National Park and Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake
Powell, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County and Zion National Park.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread moderate to at times heavy precipitation is expected
across much of southern, southeast and east central Utah tonight
through Sunday.

Moist antecedent conditions from recent heavy rains will result
in efficient and excessive runoff, allowing all area washes,
streams and rivers to run fast and high. Flood prone areas will
likely become inundated at times, and backcountry roads will
likely become impassable from this excessive runoff.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
